title: The Chief reason for the rule
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：chief　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chief 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the musician wrote of ① a chief reason for the rule in the programme, and everybody in the hall said at once that it was ② so chief that nobody in the hall would go near it. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the musician, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the chief ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the chief reason for the rule that anybody there had ever seen, or so the programme for December 1953 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too chief to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the chief ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a chief engineer on the site, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as chief as the engineer on the site they had once had in the old hall. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was chief or not, and he said so.

By 1966 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something chief, and nothing besides. The listener from the next hall called the whole plan ⑧ quite chief; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the chief ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1969, in silence, she wrote of another chief reason for the rule in the same programme, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ no less chief than anybody had expected. ⑩ The chief engineer on the site that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1971, was the one she could never quite name; the chief ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 主要（前置定语 a chief reason for the rule：1959 年乐师在节目单里记下的那件主要的缘由）
B. adj. 主要／首席（两处加强说法：so chief that … 与 no less chief than …）
C. adj. 主要／首席（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 主要（表语 too chief to do：母亲觉得它太主要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 首席（前置定语 a chief engineer on the site：叔叔把整件事称作一桩首席的总工程师）
F. adj. 首席（同级比较 as chief as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩工地上的总工程师相比）
G. adj. 首席（后置定语 something chief：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 首席（受程度副词修饰 quite chief：那位听客的评价）

items.q: a chief reason for the rule
the chief reason for the rule that
a chief engineer on the site
The chief engineer on the site that

answers.why: chief 意为“主要”，1959 年乐师在节目单里记下的是“一件主要的缘由”，此处作前置定语 a chief reason for the rule。
chief 意为“主要”，此处用 so chief that 结构，说它主要到音乐厅里没人敢靠近。
chief 意为“主要”，节目单上 十二月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的主要那条规矩的缘由，等于最高级的说法。
chief 意为“主要”，母亲认为这件东西“太主要了，谁也用不上”，too chief to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
chief 意为“首席”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩首席的总工程师”，此处作前置定语 a chief engineer on the site。
chief 意为“首席”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩工地上的总工程师一样首席”，同级比较用 as chief as。
chief 意为“首席”，节目单上那半行字要的是“首席的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something chief。
chief 意为“首席”，邻音乐厅来的那位听客认为这套计划“相当首席”，quite 修饰原级 chief。
chief 意为“首席”，no less chief than 表示“其首席不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之首席不亚于任何人的预料。
chief 意为“首席”，母亲 1971 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的首席总工程师”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1959 年，乐师在节目单里记下了一件主要的缘由。（a chief reason for the rule）
它主要到音乐厅里没有一个人敢靠近。（so chief that …）
母亲觉得它太主要，谁也用不上。（too chief to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩首席的总工程师。（a chief engineer on the site）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩工地上的总工程师一样首席。（as chief as …）
到了 1966 年，节目单上只剩半行字：要的是一件首席的东西。（something chief）
answers: In 1959 the musician wrote of a chief reason for the rule in the programme.
It was so chief that nobody in the hall would go near it.
My mother thought it too chief to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a chief engineer on the site.
He said nobody would call it as chief as the engineer on the site they had once had.
By 1966 the programme asked for nothing but something chief.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 chief 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the musician wrote of a chief reason for the rule in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the chief reason for the rule that anybody there had ever seen, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too chief to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a chief engineer on the site, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next hall called the plan quite chief, and everybody laughed.
The chief ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
